title: Dictionary Entries
description: Look at the dictionary entries below. Use the information provided to complete the sentences.

entries.definition: a substance that makes air, water, or soil dirty and not suitable or safe to use
bullet_points: Environmental scientists identified plastic microfibers [as a major pollutant] threatening coastal wildlife.
Heavy vehicle exhaust is recognized as a common [air pollutant] in crowded downtown streets.
Old thermal power stations can [release a pollutant] into nearby freshwater reservoirs.
The agricultural inspection team detected a [dangerous chemical pollutant] in the farmland drainage canal.

questions.text: Smoggy factory chimneys pump particulate matter into the sky, making it a hazardous __________ that causes lung disease.
Strict environmental laws prevent manufacturing factories from having the right to __________ into public streams.

entries.definition: to break down gradually into smaller parts through natural, chemical, or biological processes
bullet_points: Beneficial soil microbes and earthworms [help decompose organic matter] into nutrient-rich humus.
Thick cardboard packaging takes several humid months [to decompose slowly] in a backyard garden.
Most cotton canvas fabrics [can decompose over time] without leaving synthetic toxic residues behind.
Fruit peelings and dry garden leaves will [decompose naturally] when buried in aerated soil.

questions.text: Adding red wriggler worms to your compost barrel will __________ much faster than ordinary aeration alone.
Dense wooden tree bark requires many rainy seasons __________ beneath the forest floor before turning into rich loam.

entries.definition: able to continue or be continued for a long time without damaging the environment
bullet_points: Switching municipal bus fleets entirely to electricity [is economically sustainable] over a ten-year operational period.
Crop rotation and drip irrigation are traditional techniques supporting [sustainable agriculture] in rural valleys.
Local timber companies are legally required to manage forestry reserves [in a sustainable manner] without clear-cutting.
Biodegradable seaweed wraps offer an innovative, [sustainable alternative to plastics] for packaging fresh groceries.

questions.text: Natural bamboo cutlery provides a durable, __________ when packing takeaway lunches.
Farmers adopting organic fertilisation and solar water pumps contribute greatly to __________ across the countryside.

entries.definition: an object such as a box, bottle, or jar that can be used for holding something
bullet_points: Mai washed an aluminium [container for food leftovers] before putting it in her school backpack.
Customers who purchase package-free detergents must [use a container] brought from home.
Keep dried pantry herbs and spices in a labelled [storage container] to prevent moisture damage.
Laboratory researchers placed biological specimens inside a firmly [sealed glass container] on the sterilised bench.

questions.text: Shoppers visiting zero-waste bulk grocery stores are asked to __________ rather than purchasing disposable plastic wraps.
To preserve homemade raspberry jam without spoiling, pour the warm mixture into a __________.

entries.definition: to fill something again after it has been emptied or partly emptied
bullet_points: Modern airport transit lounges provide filtered water stations so passengers can easily [refill bottles] before flying.
If your metal flasks are empty, you [can refill them] at the hallway drinking fountain free of charge.
Customers at the neighborhood beverage kiosk are encouraged [to refill cups] rather than requesting disposable mugs.
Athletes at the marathon finish line quickly [refill containers with water] to rehydrate after running.

questions.text: Volunteers setting up the hydration booth at the park marathon must __________ before runners cross the finish line.
The university cafeteria offers a ten-percent drink discount to students who bring mugs __________.
